newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italian, Greek troops reach troubled Albanian city.
newsitem.headline: Italian, Greek troops reach troubled Albanian city.

text.p: Heavily armed Italian and Greek troops poured into the violent southern Albanian port city of Vlore on Monday and secured a key bridgehead with a spectacular show of force.

Nearly a week after soldiers from a multinational security force secured two key ports of entry, Italian and Greek troops drove into Vlore early on Monday as Italian marines splashed ashore in a seaborne landing.
About 30 tanks and armoured personnel carriers rolled onto beaches near the port after amphibious landing craft brought them to shore from a transport ship.

Some 160 Italian marines leaped off their launches and hovercraft. With rifles at the ready position, they immediately began searching buildings near the port as sporadic gunfire rattled in the distance.
"The operation went exactly according to plan," said Italian commanding officer Colonel Vincenzo Lops.
Vlore, 150 km (90 miles south of Tirana), and much of southern Albania have been controlled by rebel committees since an armed uprising that has claimed about 300 lives began in February.
The committees reject the authority of President Sali Berisha and demand his resignation. They blame Berisha for the collapse of get-rich-quick schemes that triggered the revolt.

The eight-nation U.N.-backed security force that will protect humanitarian aid convoys had been extraordinarily cautious about its plans for entering Vlore, where the violence began and the death toll has been high.
The troops were the first permanent contingent of soldiers into Vlore from the 6,000-strong force.
About 4,000 soldiers have now arrived in Albania. France, Spain, Romania, Turkey, Austria and Denmark are also contributing troops.
"On Tuesday the troops might, and I would like to emphasize the word 'might,' start accompanying the first aid convoys," said Gianfranco Scala, spokesman for the military command in Tirana.
General Girolamo Giglio said a total of 740 troops arrived in Vlore on Monday. He said 450 Italian and 130 Greek soldiers came by land and another 160 Italians by sea.
Hundreds of Albanians watched from a distance as the sea landing unfolded. Many cheered and tried to shake the hands of the soldiers after they arrived and fanned out through the area.
"Our brothers, the Italians," they chanted. "We're glad our brothers have come."
Fresh violence broke out in the capital Tirana on Tuesday. A 34-year-old father of four was shot dead by five gunmen as he stood guard at a glass factory on the western outskirts, police said.
Another, 29-year-old man, was killed by three gunmen for what a police spokesman called "property reasons."
The state news agency ATA reported a Vlore man was shot dead on Monday evening by a man who was trying to steal his car.
In Rome, Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said Italy considered it vital for Albania's planned general election to go ahead by the end of June.
"Rapid and transparent elections to allow the immediate removal of troops and to confirm that the crisis is temporary are essential," Prodi said.
In Vienna, Albanian Foreign Minister Arjan Starova said the general election would be held as promised on June 29 because the government was regaining control in the south.
The situation in Albania had largely improved with public order restored in most parts of the country, said Starova, a member of the centre-left Social Democratic Union.
